about: Tasks to try the skill on, in the same shape as the vendored nuvui evals: a one-line prompt, the packages installed, and regular expressions for what the written files should and shouldn't contain. A match is a first look only; the result still has to pass `pnpm lint` (Biome + stylelint) and `pnpm build`.

evals.prompt: Style the InvoiceCard component: a bordered card with the invoice number, the total on the right on wider screens, and a red border when it's overdue.

expect.why: One global block file beside the component, imported by it.
The block class is named after the component in kebab-case.
Elements are nested one level with &__.
The overdue state is a modifier on the block.
The red comes from the semantic danger token.
The wider-screen layout uses nuvui's breakpoint mixin, smallest screen first.
The modifier is added next to the base class, not instead of it.

reject.why: The convention is global BEM files, not CSS Modules.
A color written out instead of a token.
Never needed: app CSS is unlayered and beats nuvui's layers.
Smallest screen first; no max-width queries.

evals.prompt: Make the buttons in our page toolbar fully rounded, but only in the toolbar.

expect.why: A nuvui component's look changes through its --nuv-* variable.
The value is a radius token.

reject.why: Never target a nuv- class with a selector.
A raw value where a token exists.

evals.prompt: Change the app's primary color to our green brand color and make sure dark mode still looks right.

expect.why: Re-theme by setting nuvui's own token name.
Dark values go through nuvui's dark mixin, which follows data-theme.
Token overrides live in one theme file under styles/base.

reject.why: data-theme handles system dark mode; don't write the media query by hand.
Token overrides stay unlayered so they win over nuvui's tokens layer.
nuvui has no theme provider; dark mode is an attribute.
